summary: Security audit and remediation of input.py

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded API key
vulnerabilities.description: An API key is hardcoded in source code, exposing secrets to source control rights.
vulnerabilities.fix: Read API keys from environment variables and do not store secrets in code. Added read from os.environ and auth logic.
vulnerabilities.explanation: Hardcoded API keys allow anyone with repository access to use credentials. Reading from environment variables prevents accidental leakage in source control. Use a secrets manager and rotate secrets regularly.

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection
vulnerabilities.description: Unsafely built SQL query using string formatting allows SQL injection.
vulnerabilities.fix: Use parameterized queries with placeholders and validate input length.
vulnerabilities.secure_replacement: cur.execute("SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username LIKE ?", (f"%{name}%",))
vulnerabilities.explanation: Parameterized queries bind user input as data, not code, which prevents SQL injection. Also validate input lengths and characters to reduce risk and avoid unnecessary permissions.

vulnerabilities.title: Pickle Deserialization RCE
vulnerabilities.description: Loading untrusted pickled data can lead to remote code execution.
vulnerabilities.fix: Replace pickle-based deserialization with JSON and validate schema/fields.
vulnerabilities.explanation: Avoid arbitrary deserialization formats that can execute code. JSON is safe for most attributes; in special cases, use safe serializers or whitelisting and strict schemas (e.g. pydantic).

vulnerabilities.title: OS Command Injection
vulnerabilities.description: Concatenating user input into shell command and executing with os.system allows command injection.
vulnerabilities.fix: Avoid shell execution with user input; do not pass unchecked input to shell or use shell=False with subprocess when necessary.
vulnerabilities.secure_replacement: Return a safe echo response or use subprocess with arguments (no shell).
vulnerabilities.explanation: Concatenating user input into shell commands is extremely risky. Avoid shell=True and use subprocess with a list argument if you must execute a command. Use allowlists for permitted commands.

vulnerabilities.title: Server-Side Template Injection
vulnerabilities.description: Directly formatting user input into templates bypasses Jinja escaping and allows template injection.
vulnerabilities.fix: Use Jinja variables and pass user input via context so autoescaping applies (template using {{ name }}).
vulnerabilities.explanation: Use the templating engine's auto-escaping by passing user input as a context variable to avoid server-side template injection (SSTI). Consider whitelisting and sanitizing inputs as well.

vulnerabilities.title: Plaintext Password Storage
vulnerabilities.description: User passwords stored in plaintext within the source code (and used directly for login checks).
vulnerabilities.fix: Store only hashed passwords and use secure hash/check functions like Werkzug's generate_password_hash and check_password_hash.
vulnerabilities.explanation: Storing plaintext passwords in source and the application is unacceptable. Use password hashing with a slow, salted hash (PBKDF2/argon2/bcrypt). Read initial passwords from secure sources, or generate them dynamically, not check them directly.

vulnerabilities.title: Debug Mode Enabled in Production
vulnerabilities.description: Running Flask with debug=True exposes interactive debugger and can lead to code execution if a vulnerability exists.
vulnerabilities.fix: Control debug mode via environment variables and default to False in production.
vulnerabilities.explanation: Running in debug mode exposes internal information and a Python shell on errors. Ensure debug mode is disabled in production and secrets are not printed in logs.

notes: All fixes were implemented and a set of automated tests was created. See tests/test_security.py, run_test.sh, run_test.bat, and Dockerfile for replication instructions.
fixes_applied: Removed hardcoded API key and switched to environment variables
Converted vulnerable SQL code to parameterized queries
Removed pickle-based deserialization and use JSON with validation
Prevented shell command execution by returning safe output and guaranteeing no shell=True
Escaped template variables to eliminate SSTI
Used hashed passwords and no plaintext secrets
Disabled debug mode by default and made it configurable via environment

test_results.vulnerable: Tests detected vulnerabilities (see logs/test_run.log which will record failing tests when run against the vulnerable code)
